terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. A southern Thai prayer hall inside a walled compound. A whitewashed courtyard wall with a proud coping and a flat-topped gate block carrying a raised border and a Moorish doorway; a white hall 11.0 x 9.9 x 5.46 m whose front is an open five-bay Moorish loggia -- three doorways between two blind niches on a pale green field -- under a cornice ledge, a parapet with a green band and a white coping; a square podium and a round drum with twelve pointed windows carrying the great ribbed dome and its gilt crescent; four small ribbed domes on ringed drums at the roof corners; and a square tapering minaret engaged with the left wall, with a corbelled octagonal balcony, an eight-arch lantern, a ribbed dome and a crescent.

reasoning: The registry notes name the recognisable pairing exactly -- ONE large ribbed dome plus a single slender minaret -- and the proxy places the minaret ENGAGED with the hall's left wall rather than free-standing in the courtyard, which is where the first build put it.
Six ribbed domes across three systems, a five-bay Moorish loggia with three real openings, a twelve-window drum, an eight-arch minaret lantern, and a walled courtyard with a gate.
Four materials carry weathering as post-construction canvas tiles; the dome carries two measured colours through per-vertex rib striping.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The loggia is a REAL recess: the arched screen wall stands 1.8 m in front of the pale green inner wall, roofed by the same slab, so the three doorways read as openings from every azimuth rather than as dark panels painted on a solid block.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

resolvedUnknowns: The loggia is on the +Z elevation only; the other three elevations are plain render. The plate shows one arcaded face and one plain face, and the proxy's other two depth maps are plain.
ONE minaret, engaged with the left wall as the proxy places it. The plate shows one.
The loggia is 1.8 m deep and stops at a pale green inner wall; there is no interior beyond it. This prop is an exterior shell.

The gate is centred on the front run. The proxy centres it; the plate's off-centre gate sits on a front wall drawn 30 degrees off the hall's own front, the projective drift a generated plate carries, and the hall's centre arch and the gate line up on the plate itself.

preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 14.00 x 12.00 x 16.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=32000 triangles, <=24 draw calls, <=16 materials, <=32 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Static landmark geometry: nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and gets no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the compound, not with the minaret separately.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares, +Y up, loggia facing +Z. The hall is offset toward the back of the courtyard (z -5.90..+4.00, from the proxy side map), which is what the plate shows: a deeper forecourt in front of the arcade than behind the hall. The minaret centre is x -5.05, z -2.90 -- the proxy TOP map puts its shaft at cols 15-24 and rows -0.18..-0.24 H -- so its shaft stands 0.07-0.21 m proud of the left wall and rises through the parapet.

silhouette.description: A low walled compound to 1.65 m, a wide low hall to 5.46 m, a drum and a ribbed dome to 9.50 m with a gilt cap, ball, spike and crescent to 10.85 m, four small domes at the roof corners to 7.55 m, and an engaged minaret to 12.00 m. The silhouette events are the great dome, the minaret, the loggia rhythm and the corner-dome cluster.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -7.05..+7.05 and z spans -8.05..+8.05, the courtyard wall plus its 5 cm coping on the declared 14 x 16 footprint. y spans 0.00 to 11.998, the top of the MINARET's crescent. The height is the SECOND BUILD's correction: the first shipped 18 m on the registry notes' word alone, and the Meshy proxy read with scratch/_mon/vox.mjs and front.mjs spans 1.77 x 1.90 units in plan against 1.447 tall, so at 14 x 16 m the compound is 11.6-12.3 m high (mean 12.0). The declaration was corrected to 12 m with that arithmetic in the registry notes before this build, and every height here is a row of the proxy depth maps at 69.75 px/m: hall parapet 5.46 (row 456), dome crown 9.50 (row 175), corner domes 7.18 (row 336), minaret balcony 9.10 (side map row 190).
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate, compared band by band with scratch/_mon/bands.mjs (area-weighted surface sampling, 5-95 pct width and depth per tenth of height): mean |delta width| 0.026 and |delta depth| 0.032 of height, against 0.300 / 0.243 for the first build. Bands 2-9 agree within 0.036 on width; the two residuals are band 0, where the candidate reads 1.097 against 1.206 because the thin courtyard wall carries little of the sampled surface and the 95th percentile falls inside it, and band 7-8 depth (+0.07 / +0.04) where the minaret lantern and the dome ornament span slightly more z than the proxy's.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.65: the compound is bilaterally symmetric and the domes are surfaces of revolution, but the LOGGIA is on one elevation only and the minaret is on one side, so the rear and the right side are authored as plain streaked render, which is what the proxy's -Z and +X depth maps show.

localOverrides.region: walls, streaked from the coping DOWN
localOverrides.evidence: The plate's dirt runs the OPPOSITE way from every other prop in the batch: black rain-wash hangs from every coping and cornice, measuring #8C8776 in a streak at (560,520) against #C9C6C0 on clean render beside it -- a ratio of 0.69, drawn at 0.50 alpha-faded. The tile's v is keyed to the TOP of each part, so the mould band and the drips land on the coping of the hall, the court wall and the minaret alike, at their own heights.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-render (PBR confidence 0.773) at #B2B2AE on a lit courtyard wall; the plate's clean coping reads #D8D6D1 and its streaked upper walls #938F85. Authored at #B4B4B0 with the weathering tile multiplying it down: on matched windows the render's front field means 169 against the plate's lit 199 and its side wall 149 against the plate's shaded 121 -- the harness has a flatter key than the plate, and the two windows straddle it.
Shared by the courtyard wall, the hall, the arcade surrounds, the drum, the corner drums and the minaret -- six consumers, one render.
Textureless as declared: the weathering is a post-construction Canvas 2D tile (map + bumpMap, multiplier space over white) bound after construction, not a procedural texture set.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

The extractor palette is advisory only: these crops are flat material swatches, not isolated objects, so its foreground separation is weak by its own warnings. Albedo is the direct crop measurement.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-dome (PBR confidence 0.860). The material colour is the RIB CREST, authored at #939A86 against the measured #9BA08D; the green valleys come from a per-vertex multiplier of (0.30, 0.39, 0.32) in LINEAR space off the same cosine that shapes the rib, with the crest narrowed to about a quarter of the pitch (exponent 0.35) as the plate at 3x shows. On a matched window the dome renders at mean luma 140.6 against the plate's 133.9, from 148.8 at the first build's tones.
Textureless: the stripe is geometry-driven vertex colour, which is exactly the case the procedural texture set is not needed for.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

repetitionSystems.name: Arcade surrounds
repetitionSystems.rationale: Three surrounds over the three doorways at one geometry and one submission.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Each surround is a plate with a REAL aperture 0.02 m smaller than the screen's opening, extruded from 0.40 m inside the screen to 0.05 m proud of the green field, so it lines the reveal and overlaps the field's hole edge.

repetitionSystems.name: Corner dome drums
repetitionSystems.rationale: Four drums with their moulded top ring at one geometry.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Each springs from the deck top at 5.06, 0.62 m below the great dome's podium lip, and its ring is wider than its drum.

repetitionSystems.name: Corner domes
repetitionSystems.rationale: Twenty ribs each, four instances, one geometry and one draw call. They carry the same per-vertex crest-and-valley striping as the great dome.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Each springs from 6.18, 0.04 m below its ring top, so it overhangs rather than meeting a plane.

acceptance: Silhouette reads correctly without materials.
Quality contract has named all required macro feature groups before code generation.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Build the component hierarchy implied by the pre-spec complexity assessment.
acceptance: Macro, meso, and repeated structures meet qualityContract.minimumSpecDepth.
Parent-child relations, joints, seams, sockets, and contact points are explicit.
Every attached child appendage/connector has parentSocket, localStart/localEnd, contactType, embedDepth or overlap, and gapTolerance.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Refine shape, deformation, bevels, tapers, curves, asymmetry, and visible local geometry.
acceptance: Important visible forms are represented in component geometryDescriptor, deformations, localFeatures, or repetitionSystems.
Endpoint-based child parts are rooted at their attachment sockets and do not visibly float away from parents.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.
acceptance: Reference-derived albedo palette records dominant, secondary, and accent colors per visible material.
Each important material defines roughness variation and at least one normal/bump/displacement response.
Local material overrides, dirt/wear/stains/moss/chips/scratches or equivalent masks are tied to evidenceRefs.
Thin, transparent, reflective, wet, or fibrous materials document alpha/transmission/clearcoat/metalness/fiber response when relevant.
Generated preview uses procedural albedo/roughness/bump texture or vertex color variation instead of one flat color.
Generated preview uses independent PBR maps at 1024px or higher for the quality-first tier.
If source pixels are available, referencePbr extraction passed at confidence >= 0.7 or the pass is stopped/requesting better references.
Macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands are visible at the intended review distance without obvious tiling.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Add procedural surface locality such as normal/bump/displacement, AO, dirt, stains, chips, grain, moss, scratches, and wear.
acceptance: Every required material feature group has local overrides or surfaceDetail tied to evidenceRefs.
A grazing-angle close-up proves that normal/height detail breaks highlights naturally and does not read as smooth plastic.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make material and form readable under neutral turntable lighting plus optional reference lighting.
acceptance: lightingFromPhoto identifies key light direction/color/intensity, fill light, rim or environment light, and ambient color.
Exposure, tone mapping, background color/gradient, shadow softness, and contact shadow behavior are specified.
Lighting does not hide geometry/material gaps and screenshots can be compared fairly to the reference.
Neutral, grazing, and reference-matched lighting checks distinguish material errors from lighting errors.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Make the model ready for future animation, transformation, physics, or destruction.
acceptance: Macro and movable meso components have stable pivot nodes.
Sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata are present for future runtime actions.
AI vision comparison score meets selfCorrectLoop.visualAcceptance.threshold.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.
acceptance: Triangle count, draw calls, instancing, LOD strategy, and FPS target are documented or verified.
Repeated detail is instanced or simplified where possible without breaking silhouette/material believability.

reviewHistory.summary: Blockout: ten components and 3 InstancedMesh systems at 13 draw calls of 24. Every height a row of the proxy depth maps at 69.75 px/m; the hall 11.0 x 9.9 x 5.46 on a 12.0 m compound, the declared height corrected from 18 with the arithmetic in the asset notes.

Rebuilt after promotion at 0.81. The declared 18 m built a 7.95 m cube of a hall on a 9.2 m plan under a free-standing minaret, and the silhouette layer scored 0.74 against a proxy that reads the same plate at 12 m. The proxy read with vox.mjs and front.mjs -- compound 1.77 x 1.90 units in plan against 1.447 tall, hall 11.0 m wide to a 5.46 m parapet, dome r 2.40 with its crown at 9.50, minaret engaged with the left wall -- and the declaration corrected to 12 m with the arithmetic in the asset notes before the rebuild.

The front is an open LOGGIA, not five dark panels on a solid block: the plate's arcade crop at 3x shows piers casting shadows onto a pale green wall two metres behind them, and the proxy's +Z depth map reads the openings 1.6-2.1 m behind the face. The screen wall is one extrusion with three arch holes, the inner wall is a real surface in its own material, and the blind niches keep the field with a raised inner panel.

reviewHistory.summary: Material pass: 7 materials at PBR confidence 0.751-0.860. A pale green field material added for the loggia (0.860); the white lifted to #B4B4B0 and the dome crest to #939A86 with valleys at (0.30, 0.39, 0.32) linear, probed on matched windows against the plate: dome 140.6 vs 133.9.

Weathering as three seeded canvas tiles keyed to the top of each part. The first render of this build showed leopard-spot mottle and no streaks: CanvasTexture flips Y by default, so the streak band drawn at the tile's top row landed one tile-height BELOW every wall. flipY = false, the hard random-walk blotches replaced by wide soft mottle, and the streak count cut from 84 to 53 per 6 m tile in three length populations so the curtain reads as the plate's clusters rather than a comb.

CanvasTexture.flipY had to be false for that keying to hold.

Lighting pass: no rim light and no contact shadow in the plate; both recorded absent. Exposure 1.0, ACES filmic. The brass carries metalness 0.30 rather than physical because the harness supplies no environment map.
Interaction pass: ONE pivot (root, base-center), ZERO sockets, one BOX collider matching the declaration, no destruction groups matching the empty declared list.

featureReviews.evidence: Great dome r 2.40 on a r 2.25 drum with twelve pointed windows, crown at 9.50, crescent to 10.85; a square tapering minaret (1.32 -> 1.04 m) engaged with the left wall at x -5.05 z -2.90, corbelled octagonal balcony at 9.10, eight-arch lantern to 10.50, ribbed dome and crescent to 12.00. Band table against the Meshy proxy: bands 5-9 (the dome and minaret zone) agree within 0.033 on width; the first build's bands 5-8 were off by 0.16-0.36.
featureReviews.notes: The first build stood the minaret CLEAR of the hall at x -5.75 because the registry notes said so; the proxy's TOP map puts its shaft inside the hall's left edge (cols 15-24, rows -0.18..-0.24 H) and the plate's shaft rises from behind the roof with no base visible, which is an engaged tower. Residual: the ornament and lantern span 0.04-0.07 of height more in z than the proxy's at bands 7-8.

featureReviews.evidence: Three 1.55 m Moorish doorways (shoulder 2.65, apex 3.85, from proxy rows 650 / 570) cut through a 0.6 m screen wall onto an open loggia 1.8 m deep, its inner wall the pale green the plate paints it (#B8C1AA lit, PBR confidence 0.860); two narrower blind niches at +-4.15 with a white surround and a raised inner arch panel on the same green field. The front turntable frame shows the inner wall through every opening at luma well above the backdrop.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's arcade was five dark panels PROUD of a solid block, because 'the hall is a solid mass'. The plate's arcade crop at 3x shows the piers casting shadows onto a wall two metres behind them, and the proxy's +Z depth map reads the openings 1.6-2.1 m behind the face. Residual: the plate's loggia floor and inner wall carry their own shading the harness's flatter key does not reproduce.

featureReviews.evidence: Four ribbed corner domes r 1.00 on ringed drums at (+-4.18, -4.40 / +2.50) -- the proxy's 801 px and side-map 225 / 675 px -- with tops at 7.16 against the proxy's 7.18; gilt spikes; the cap-ball-bulb-spike-crescent stack over the great dome and, at 0.4 scale, over the minaret. Corner drums spring from the deck at 5.06, 0.62 m below the great dome's podium lip.
featureReviews.notes: The corner domes now stand at the roof CORNERS on drums the deck can be seen under, where the first build's sat at +-3.40 on a 9.2 m hall. Residual: the plate's corner drums carry a small moulded base ring this build folds into the drum's top ring.

featureReviews.evidence: Turntable gate run with --allow-holes and the measurement that justifies it: the enclosed-background components at 090 and 270 are the COURTYARD (14,302 px, 125 x 153 bbox, mean thickness 93 px), and at 000 the courtyard strips either side of the hall (3,768 px, 19 px thick). Nothing enclosed is a surface of the model.
featureReviews.notes: A walled compound has real open ground between its enclosure wall and its hall, and from any three-quarter view the silhouette encloses that background on all four sides. The flag is set on that finding rather than to get past an unexplained failure, as in the first build; the loggia openings themselves land on the lit inner wall and are not flagged.

featureReviews.evidence: Seven materials at PBR confidence 0.751-0.860, every albedo measured off the plate; three seeded canvas tiles carry the rain-wash from the TOP of every part down. Matched windows: dome mean luma 140.6 against the plate's 133.9; front field 169 against the plate's lit 199 and side wall 149 against its shaded 121 (the harness has a flatter key than the plate and the two windows straddle it); deck 154 against 107, the plate's window including its own shadowed stains.
featureReviews.notes: The first build carried the streak DIRECTION as a vertex gradient and no streaks. The tile's v is keyed to each part's top, which needed CanvasTexture.flipY = false -- with the default flip the whole streak band landed a tile-height below every wall and only the mottle showed, as leopard spots. Residual: the plate's streaks cluster; the tile's are more even.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.92 -- not a pass self-score. Second build: the declared 18 m corrected to the proxy's 12, and the hall, loggia, drum, corner domes and engaged minaret all re-authored off the proxy depth maps and the plate crops at 3x. Band table 0.026 / 0.032 of height. 17,088/32,000 triangles, 13/24 draw calls, 7/16 materials, 13/32 unique geometries.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero4x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Ten components and three repetition systems: 13 of 24. The drum windows and the lantern openings share one dark material and are merged into one component rather than instanced, because they are two different plate sizes; the blind niches are merged into the hall for the same reason, leaving the three doorway surrounds as the only instanced arch.

materials.note: white covers the courtyard wall, the hall, the arcade surrounds, the drum, the corner drums AND the minaret -- six consumers, one render. Seven of sixteen materials; the dome material carries two measured colours by itself through vertex striping, and the pale green field is the one addition this build needed, because the loggia's inner wall is now a lit surface.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 17,088 of 32,000, and nearly all of it is domes: six ribbed surfaces at 96, 64 and 48 radial samples. That is the correct place to spend it -- the ribs are what make a dome a mosque dome at the distance a village skyline is read from -- and the draw-call axis is at half its ceiling.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Ribbed surfaces of revolution, Moorish-arch extrusions with holes, an extruded U plan, octagonal prisms, a lathe ring, a flat crescent extrusion and boxes. The arched screen wall is ONE extrusion of a rectangle carrying three arch holes, which is what makes the loggia a real recess at no extra draw call.

Three InstancedMesh systems carry 11 of the prop's discrete parts. The corner domes carry their rib striping through the same per-vertex attribute as the great dome, so instancing costs the stripe nothing.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. Three seeded Canvas 2D tiles -- render, pale green and screed -- are bound as map and bumpMap AFTER construction, in multiplier space over white, with v keyed to the top of each part so the mould band and drips hang from every coping; under Node there is no canvas and the materials render their flat measured colour. The dome striping is per-vertex colour off the same cosine that shapes the rib.

risks.description: The registry declared 18 m for two builds; the proxy and the plate agree on 12. The correction is recorded in the asset notes with its arithmetic.
risks.mitigation: Every height in this build is a row of the proxy depth maps at 69.75 px/m, and the band comparison against the proxy is 0.026 / 0.032 of height.

risks.description: The rain-wash is a seeded tile, so its streaks repeat every 6 m along a wall and are more even than the plate's clustered ones.
risks.mitigation: Three drip populations at different lengths and widths, offset per material and per part in u, so no two parts carry the same column of streaks.
